text:
Mike: quick sync — pushing a proposal to try a 'snooze window' for noncritical autoscale this week to smooth costs during the EU marketing surge :chart_with_downwards_trend:
Anya: can you sketch the policy? sounds like pausing burst replicas for X mins after a spike?
Mike: yep. idea: when short burst detected (<12m), tag as "snooze_candidate" and avoid provisioning spot/burst for 15m unless queue backlog > threshold. fallback still allowed for p95 latency breaches.
Prasad: i like the idea but need numbers. what's the threshold and expected GPU-hours saved?
Mike: rough calc: during last promo EU spike we saw 1.2k GPU-hours over 6h attributable to microbursts. If we snooze for 15m on microbursts we estimate ~22% reduction of that slice -> ~260 GPU-hours saved.
Elaine: 260 GPU-hours in EU at current committed price is about $9k. But consider risk: if snooze blocks necessary capacity and causes retries we could cost more in request retries/failed jobs.
Anya: can we limit snooze to specific job tags (inference-low-prio, batch-shadow) and keep chat/hosted routes exempt?
Mike: yes, plan is route-aware. hosted/chat routes are exempt. only apply to groups: batch-infer, async-embeddings, rerank-low.
Prasad: what about zones? we saw most burst provisioning came from eu-west1 cluster-a and eu-west2 cluster-b. apply per-cluster rule?
Mike: per-cluster thresholds. For eu-west1-cluster-a use backlog threshold 120 reqs/min and only snooze if backlog < 45 reqs for 3 consecutive minutes.
Julia: can infra bot simulate this against last 30 days of telemetry to get false-positive rate?
InfraBot: @Julia running replay simulation for 2026-02-10..2026-03-10 on tags [batch-infer, async-embeddings]. ETA ~28m.
Elaine: also surface a cost vs risk dashboard: projected saved GPU-hours, expected p95 latency delta, and number of times fallback fired. Ops needs visibility before enabling.
Mike: agreed. dashboard fields: region, cluster, projected-saved-gpu-hrs/week, expected-p95-delta-ms, fallback-count-est.
Anya: small UX ask — mark snoozed actions in the console timeline as amber with tooltip "snooze window applied" so support doesn't escalate.
Prasad: capacity accounting — these saved GPU-hours should go back to burst pools or reduce our committed top-up? we need finance input.
Elaine: finance prefers showing saved hours as delta to committed utilization in monthly reports. but they want a safety buffer of 5% unallocated.
Mike: action list: (1) InfraBot run sim and post CSV (2) Prasad create per-cluster threshold PR to autoscaler config (3) Julia wire dashboard prototype (4) Anya update console UX flags (5) Elaine loop in finance.
Prasad: i'll open the PR after InfraBot sim. expecting threshold tweaks after we see sim false positives.
InfraBot: simulation complete. results: total candidate bursts: 482, false-positives (where snooze would have triggered but p95 latency breached within 10m): 16 (3.3%), estimated saved GPU-hours: 248. CSV uploaded to https://redwood-internal/ops/sim/2523456789-snooze-sim.csv
Julia: looking at CSV — most candidates were short spikes of 2-8 minutes, eu-west1 cluster-a drove 61% of candidates.
Anya: with 3.3% FP that's acceptable. can we limit rollout to eu-west1 only for 72h canary?
Mike: propose canary: eu-west1 cluster-a only, 72h, snooze window 15m, exempt routes as discussed. then review dashboard and sim results.
Elaine: +1. finance ok with canary; they'll take reported delta into monthly comms.
Prasad: will add circuit-breaker: if p95 increases > 8% for two consecutive 15m buckets, auto-disable snooze for that cluster.
Mike: sounds good. I'll write the runbook snippet and draft the autoscaler PR text. posting a short playbook now:
```
playbook: snooze-window canary
- target: eu-west1 cluster-a
- duration: 72h
- snooze-window: 15m
- exempt-routes: hosted/chat, urgent-infer
- circuit-breaker: p95 > +8% for 2 consecutive 15m -> disable
- metrics: saved_gpu_hrs, p95_latency, fallback_count, blocked_provision_events
- postmortem owners: Prasad, Anya
```
Anya: nice. one more: notify support channel when canary flips circuit-breaker automatically.
Mike: will add webhook to #support and #eng-oncall.
Julia: i'll set up dashboard tiles. ETA 12h.
Prasad: PR incoming in ~2h.
InfraBot: canary scheduled to start 2026-03-20T02:00Z. Will post status updates to thread and #eng-infra.
Mike: thanks all. quick end note — if canary looks clean we can extend to apac non-critical clusters with shorter window (10m) because we saw shorter bursts there.
Elaine: noted. we'll also add a finance checkpoint after first full week. :money_with_wings:
